newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges down in thin trade.

text.p: The average lending rate edged down on Tuesday to 8.5 percent from 9.6 percent amid slow trade and high supply of kuna funds on the interbank market.
Total settlements fell to a modest 12.5 million kuna, of which only 5 million were new kuna funds, against a supply of 125 million kuna, traders said.
Demands for 5-10 and 10-15 day loans were met at 7.0 percent. Loans for 15-30 days were flat at 12.0 percent.
Call money was unchanged at 8.0 percent and insurers' short-term rate was steady at 7.0 percent.
Overnight trade totalled 0.7 million kuna against a 404 million kuna supply, as only one bank with shortfalls needed funds to square its position.

The central bank stayed out of the hard currency market on Tuesday. Its kuna mid-rates for Wednesday firmed to 5,3822 from 5,3993 against the dollar and eased slightly to 3,5601 from 3.5599 against the mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
